results.title: Occupational health and safety issues in human-robot collaboration
results.content: # Occupational health and safety issues in human-robot collaboration: State of the art and open challenges. Overview on Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) concerns in collaborative environments. Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC) refers to the interaction of workers and robots in a shared workspace. Although the overall safety of collaborative robotics has increased over time, further research efforts are needed to allow humans to operate alongside robots, with awareness and trust. Numerous safety concerns are open, and either new or enhanced technical, procedural and organizational measures have to be investigated to design and implement inherently safe and ergonomic automation solutions, aligning the systems performance and the human safety. Human-centered design and cognitive engineering principles also require further investigations to increase the worker acceptance and trust during collaboration. Whatever the application context is, the implementation of more and more advanced technologies is fundamental to overcome the current HRC safety concerns, designing low-risk HRC systems while ensuring the system productivity.
